items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I never knew who the musicians were in this orchestra, but me and everyone that heard them knew that we had heard one of the best jazz orchestras that had come to town in those days

ctx.x: At that time, there was no books on jazz and the musicians that played it, so I didn't know if this Mr. "Jelly Roll" as he called himself, had done all the things he said he had. He was a pimp, gambler, hobo and pianist, but he was not looking like a hobo then and he could play piano.

Some months after, "Jelly Roll" came back to Cincinnati with the orchestra of Fate Marable. Fate played piano also but he directed the band most of the time. I never knew who the musicians were in this orchestra, but me and everyone that heard them knew that we had heard one of the best jazz orchestras that had come to town in those days, and I always found a way to hear the bands that came along.
Others that I heard in Cincy that had big names where "Speed" Webb and Alfonso Trent and Bellson, an orchestra from West Virginia and [that] Bobby Robinson and John Nesbit had played with.
